title: Inverse image and tensor product
statement:
Inverse image $g^*\colon\D(Y_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathcal O_E)\to\D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathcal O_E)$ along a morphism $g\colon X\to Y$
preserves $\Dbc(-,\mathcal O_E)$, and on these categories it agrees, after restriction of scalars to
$\underline{\mathcal O_E}$, with the completed inverse image of the Stacks Project. For
$K,L\in\Dbc(X,\mathcal O_E)$, the tensor product $K\otimes_{\mathcal O_{E,X}}^{\mathbf L}L\in\D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathcal O_E)$,
without completion, lies in $\Dbc(X,\mathcal O_E)$. Extension by zero along a quasi-compact open immersion and
direct image along a closed immersion preserve $\Dbc(-,\mathcal O_E)$.

Arguments by dévissage along a stratification need inverse image, tensor products and extension by zero
along strata to preserve integral constructible complexes; these are the statements above.

proof.text: The extension-by-zero and closed-direct-image assertions, including preservation of derived completeness and constructibility, and the finite open–closed dévissage into locally closed stratum models, are exactly the two conclusions of the existing extension/direct-image lemma.
Apply the existing integral inverse-image lemma to obtain preservation of $\Dbc$ and the comparison isomorphism with the completed Stacks inverse image after restriction of scalars.

Apply the first paragraph of the existing integral tensor-product lemma: for any $K,L\in\Dbc(X,\mathcal O_E)$, their uncompleted derived tensor product lies in $\Dbc(X,\mathcal O_E)$. Its moreover clause also states that a stratum local model is dualizable and that tensoring with it preserves products, derived inverse limits and derived complete objects, which supplies the local-model preservation used in the finite dévissage.
